case.believed: Promise.resolve is already settled so React.use reads it synchronously during renderToString, rejected promises throw out of the render, and renderToPipeableStream waits for promise content before sending any shell markup.
contract: A native Promise.resolve starts as pending from React.use's perspective on its first renderToString call, so the Suspense fallback and renderToString-does-not-support-Suspense marker are emitted; React annotates the thenable as fulfilled on a later turn.
Rendering the same now-annotated fulfilled promise again with renderToString produces its value synchronously without the fallback.

A native rejected promise is also first observed as pending; after React annotates it as rejected, renderToString emits the Suspense fallback and a client-rendering error marker containing the rejection instead of throwing out of renderToString.
renderToPipeableStream can send a fallback shell while a React.use promise is pending, then streams the fulfilled content and completes without onError after the promise resolves.
case.goal: Prove React 19.2.8 use() promise state and Suspense behavior across renderToString and renderToPipeableStream in offline Node SSR.
